doc.description:
Driver for a PWM based rangefinder sensor Reads sensor using PWM input and outputs rangefinder distance to object in [m]
Notes: + The maximum useful detection distance is 4m for common rangefinder PWM output signal small sized sensors, even if datasheet e.g. states 7m. For most PWM of the ultrasonic type of devices, a sampling rate of at least 10Hz is supported. However, if measurements are taken at longer distances, the time required for the ultrasonic pulse to return increases, which may limit the maximum achievable sampling rate. It is recommended to adjust the RANGEFINDER_PWM_PERIODIC_FREQUENCY parameter according to the sensor's capabilities and the expected measurement range to ensure reliable readings. For laser type of sensors, usually much higher sampling rates are possible, light just is a tad bit faster than sound.
+ If the distance is read but the scale is incorrect, adjust the RANGEFINDER_PWM_SCALE parameter to match the sensor's specifications. The scale factor can also be determined experimentally by measuring a known distance and adjusting the scale until the output matches the expected value.
+ If the sensor is used in an airframe with landing gear, it is recommended to set the RANGEFINDER_PWM_OFFSET to the length of the landing gear, so that the AGL value is correct. Keep in mind that most ultrasonic type of sensors have a deadzone of 0.15m to 0.25m, so the AGL cannot be measured if landinggear is shorter than the deadzone range.
+ There is an option to compensate the AGL value for body rotation, which is useful if e.g. a roll maneuver, the sensor is not pointing straight down it compensates the AGL value for the body rotation.
+ Also an option to filter the sensor output is available, which is useful if the sensor is noisy or has a lot of outliers, in case of a sonar type sensors, almost always the case. Lidar type of sensors are usually less noisy and have less outliers, so filtering better be disabled.
Why choose PWM sensor over ADC sensor: One only needs to connect GND, VCC and one more signal wire, same as ADC but not the disadvantages of ADC sensors noise
PWM Sensor example: Maxbotix LV-EZ1

configure.name: RANGEFINDER_PWM_PORT
configure.description: Select PWM input port on flightcontroller for sensor to use e.g. PWM_INPUT1

configure.name: RANGEFINDER_PWM_USE_FOR_AGL
configure.description: Updates the AGL value in state,if not defined, defaults to FALSE

configure.name: RANGEFINDER_PWM_COMPENSATE_ROTATION
configure.description: Compensate AGL measurements for body rotation. Disabled by default

define.name: RANGEFINDER_PWM_USE_FILTER
define.description: If this is enabled, a median filter on the distance output, defaults to TRUE

define.name: RANGEFINDER_PWM_MEDIAN_SIZE
define.description: If median filter is enabled then set this option to filter the output more(or less), default is 7

define.name: RANGEFINDER_PWM_SCALE
define.description: Sensor scale for raw sensor output to a meter unit conversion,

define.name: RANGEFINDER_PWM_OFFSET
define.description: Sensor offset in meters, as in where one wants zero to be for e.g. landinggear to ground, default is 0.0

define.name: RANGEFINDER_PWM_MIN_RANGE
define.description: If defined, set limit to minimum value the sensor can reliably measure, default 0.25m

define.name: RANGEFINDER_PWM_MAX_RANGE
define.description: If defined, set limit to maximum value the sensor can reliably measure, default 7.0m

define.name: RANGEFINDER_PWM_SYNC_SEND
define.description: Send RAW and scaled message with each new measurement,useful for debugging sensor issues (default: FALSE)

define.name: RANGEFINDER_PWM_PWM_PERIOD
define.description: period in microsec (e.g. 4096 for 12 bits sensor)

define.name: RANGEFINDER_PWM_PWM_OFFSET
define.description: initial offset on the raw pwm signal if needed (default: 820usec). Do not confuse this with RANGEFINDER_PWM_OFFSET
